rendered: Temperature and duration: the separated cathode powder was calcined in air at 600 °C for 2 h[1]. Purpose: the calcination was meant to remove the surface coating and the carbon black (CB) that remained on the recovered NMC622 after the Cyrene-based separation. The methods state it was done to remove sur-[2]face coatings and CB[3]. The TGA-DTG data support this choice: the organic coating layer and the CB show weight losses at ~3.3 wt% loss at ~350 °C[4] and (~4.1 wt% loss at ~550 °C)[5], and the document says they can be both removed by calcining in air[6] at 600 °C[7]. The XRD patterns before and after calcination were nearly identical with no impurity phases, indicating the layered structure of the NMC622 was retained.
